refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The systemd-tpm2-swtpm.service provides fallback software TPM functionality, intended for use in environments where a discrete or firmware TPM ("hardware TPM") is not available. It is pulled into the boot process by systemd-tpm2-generator8 if a hardware TPM is not available, and the system is configured to provide a software TPM in that case.

Note that a software TPM provides only very weak security properties compared to a hardware TPM, and hence should only be used as a fallback mechanism if a hardware TPM is not available but TPM semantics are desired. This service ultimately wraps swtpm8.

If the boot secret /.extra/boot-secret (in the initrd) or /run/systemd/stub/boot-secret (on the host) is available the software TPM NVRAM storage is encrypted with this key. See systemd-stub7 for details.
The TPM NVRAM storage is placed on the EFI System Partition as it needs to be accessible during very early boot-up, in particular before the root file system is decrypted and mounted.

If systemd.tpm2_measured_os=1 is set on the kernel command line (see kernel-command-line7), systemd-stub7 hands over the measurements it would have made without a TPM in /.extra/tpm2-event-log. In the initrd, this service replays them into the software TPM via systemd-tpm2-swtpm --replay before it is considered started, so that the PCRs systemd-stub measures into, in particular PCR 11, end up with the same values as with a hardware TPM. Signed PCR policies for the UKI then work with the software TPM, too. Measurements of the firmware, the boot loader and the kernel are not available for replay, hence the other PCRs differ from those of a hardware TPM, and so does PCR 12 if the boot loader measured a kernel command line into it, see systemd-stub7. After the transition to the host, the PCR values are retained through the state saved when the service stops in the initrd.
